editorial_candidates.excerpt: “Then f and g are transverse iff f×g:X×Z→M×M is transverse to Δ_M; the sets {(a,b):f(a)=g(b)} and (f×g)⁻¹(Δ_M) coincide.” The proof identifies T_(y,y)Δ_M={(v,v)} and quotient map (v,w)↦v−w.
editorial_candidates.why_warranted: This is a geometric equivalence of two transversality tests and their coincidence locus; a compact diagram makes the product map and diagonal preimage immediately visible.
editorial_candidates.diagram_content: Show X×Z --f×g--> M×M with Δ_M⊂M×M, label the pulled-back locus X×_M Z=(f×g)⁻¹(Δ_M)={(a,b):f(a)=g(b)}; optionally indicate the diagonal inclusion y↦(y,y). Keep the stated local sign factors in prose.
editorial_candidates.mathematical_check: The proposed arrows and preimage are exactly the Statement and [F1]–[F3]. The source fixes the diagonal orientation by the orientation-preserving map y↦(y,y), the product orientation, and the sign I(f,g)=(-1)^z I(f×g,Δ_M); these conventions must not be reversed in any diagram annotation.

editorial_candidates.excerpt: “If the attaching sphere of h^{k+1} meets the belt sphere of h^k transversely in exactly one point, then W∪h^k∪h^{k+1} is diffeomorphic to W relative to ∂₀W.” [F1] defines the cancellation as one transverse intersection point; [F4] says the standard complementary pair fills an n-disc.
editorial_candidates.why_warranted: The theorem is organized around a geometric one-point intersection criterion and local cancellation. A labeled schematic can help readers see which attaching and belt spheres intersect and what is removed.
editorial_candidates.diagram_content: Use a clearly schematic middle-boundary cross-section: the attaching sphere of the (k+1)-handle intersects the belt sphere {0}×S^{n−k−1} of the k-handle in one transverse point; show the complementary pair filling a ball and the unchanged incoming boundary ∂₀W. Label dimensions and the relative-to-∂₀W conclusion; do not imply a general low-dimensional picture or any extra sign rule.
editorial_candidates.mathematical_check: Source lines 30, 34, 36, and 42 support precisely the one-point transverse intersection, belt sphere, complementary pair, and ball filling. The diagram is an explanatory schematic for all 0≤k≤n−1, not a proof or a literal 2D realization.

editorial_candidates.excerpt: The Statement gives a bijection between framed cobordism classes of closed framed (n−k)-submanifolds of Sⁿ and πₙ(Sᵏ); [F1] defines the collapse map, and [F6] says the centre regular preimage recovers (N,φ) while collapse after regular preimage is homotopic to the original map.
editorial_candidates.why_warranted: The theorem asserts two inverse geometric constructions. A correspondence diagram can expose their direction and the two composite identities at a glance.
editorial_candidates.diagram_content: Show framed submanifold (N,φ) ↦ collapse/Thom map f_(N,φ):Sⁿ→Sᵏ and smooth map f:Sⁿ→Sᵏ ↦ framed regular preimage f⁻¹(y); annotate that the collapse of that preimage is homotopic to f and that the centre preimage of the collapse recovers (N,φ). Include n=k as a zero-dimensional/empty-preimage case if shown.
editorial_candidates.mathematical_check: Maps and inverse checks match [F1], [F6], and proof steps 2.1–2.2. The correspondence is on framed cobordism classes and homotopy classes; avoid depicting a pointwise inverse map between representatives.
